text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.1% today as oil prices climbed on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude topped $101 a barrel—its highest level since May—after reports of U.S.-Iranian military clashes and concerns that the conflict could disrupt regional energy supplies. When crude prices rise, integrated oil companies like ConocoPhillips benefit from higher margins on both production and refining.

The stock has gained 3.6% over the past two weeks as geopolitical risk has pushed crude steadily upward. The market is pricing in the possibility that tensions in the Persian Gulf, a critical chokepoint for global oil shipments, could tighten supplies further, keeping energy prices elevated through the near term.
